strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with dependent scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, where each iteration computes the sum, derives scaling factors from block means, applies scaling, reduces again, and inverts scaling. This is the reference approach with 8 all-reduce dispatches (one initial + 7 dependent iterations), trading high dispatch count for straightforward correctness and minimal local memory overhead.

strategies.name: Pipelined reduce-scatter then all-gather chain
strategies.desc: Decompose each dependent all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing partial overlap of communication phases across the 8 iterations. Results in 16 total collective dispatches (2 per iteration) but enables pipeline parallelism where reduce-scatter of iteration i+1 can overlap with all-gather of iteration i, reducing wall-clock latency at the cost of increased dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Block-parallel independent all-reduce with fusion
strategies.desc: Recognize that the 8 blocks could potentially be processed in parallel if dependencies are carefully analyzed, or batch multiple scaling operations before each all-reduce. Fuse local compute (mean calculation, ReLU, scaling) into single kernels between collectives. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local-op overhead through kernel fusion, trading implementation complexity for better compute efficiency.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploit num_nodes topology by performing intra-node reductions separately from inter-node reductions for each of the 8 dependent steps. Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 iterations × 2 levels) but smaller payloads per collective and potential bandwidth advantages from node-local communication patterns, trading dispatch count for better network utilization.

strategies.name: Batched metadata exchange with single final all-reduce
strategies.desc:
Instead of reducing full tensors 8 times, exchange only the block mean metadata (8 scalars) via all-reduce at each iteration, accumulate scaling factors locally, then perform a single all-reduce of the final scaled result. Uses 8 small all-reduces (3KB each) plus 1 large all-reduce (12KB), trading numerical precision concerns and local memory for dramatically reduced communication volume.
